claim_text: 1984 Hosting says it detected unauthorised activity in parts of its infrastructure after a targeted cyberattack
summary: 1984 Hosting says: "We recently detected unauthorized activity within parts of our infrastructure following a targeted cyberattack." It suspended its services to contain the incident.
detail: The notice was opened on its status page on Nov 21. Icelandic outlets reported the suspension on Nov 20.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The company's own status page says so in these words; DV carries its earlier statement.

claim_text: 1984 and CERT-IS said in a joint statement that it was an extensive, serious, well-organised and technically advanced attack
summary: In a joint statement with Iceland's national cyber security team, CERT-IS, carried by DV on Nov 20, 1984 said first findings pointed to a well-organised, technically advanced attack that may have reached more systems.
detail: The statement said all services were stopped for safety, with email and DNS to return first under special monitoring. It said 1984 had reported the incident to CERT-IS, which is helping investigate.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: DV prints the joint statement; the status page confirms the cyberattack and the work with CERT-IS.

claim_text: 1984 says the attackers could not see or change customer data, except on seven websites that were the original target
summary: 1984 says its investigation confirmed that the attackers "were unable to view, copy, alter, or compromise customer hosted data, with the sole exception of the 7 websites that were the original target of the attack."
detail: This finding was added to the status page on Nov 25. It is the company's own finding; nobody outside has published one.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The status page says so in these words.

claim_text: 1984's managing director says the seven damaged websites appear, from their domain names, to support Palestine
summary: 1984's managing director told Vísir that the attackers' first act after getting in was to damage seven websites that appear to support Palestine in some way. He said he sees only the domain names and cannot draw conclusions.
detail: He said he could not say whether the seven sites are Icelandic or foreign. He said 65 per cent of 1984's customers are outside Iceland.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Vísir's interview quotes him saying so.

claim_text: 1984's managing director says the attack was probably carried out by a nation-state, but names none
summary: The managing director told Vísir the attack was well planned and technically advanced, by a well-funded party, and probably the work of a nation-state. He named no country or group.
detail: No group has claimed responsibility in the reporting we read, and no official body has attributed the attack.
label: Reported

claim_text: As of Nov 26, 19:45 UTC, about 80% of 1984's virtual servers are back online, email works, and shared web hosting is due to start returning from 21:00 UTC
summary: 1984's status page (19:45 UTC, Nov 26) says about 80% of virtual servers are online, with about 95% expected by Nov 27 morning. Email has worked since Nov 24. Shared web hosting is due to return from 21:00 UTC on Nov 26.
detail: The status page still shows "Partially Degraded Service" and calls these timelines estimates. Its earlier Nov 26 update said all disks and customer data on the virtual servers are intact.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The status page's update of 19:45 UTC on Nov 26 says so.

claim_text: Iceland's Civil Protection and CERT-IS activated the national response plan for essential information infrastructure on Nov 25
summary: CERT-IS says the Civil Protection Department and CERT-IS activated the plan, at the uncertainty level, because of the growing use of AI in cyberattacks on Iceland and neighbouring countries.
detail: The CERT-IS page does not name 1984 or any other organisation. 1984's status page mentions the activation "in light of further cyberattacks against Icelandic organizations".
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: CERT-IS's own notice says so; the status page refers to it.

claim_text: CERT-IS said on Nov 26 that the alert level is unchanged and it had no report that day of a break-in by this method
summary: CERT-IS says the level stays at uncertainty. It has had many reports of probing from confirmed malicious sources where defences held, and so far that day no report of a break-in this way.
label: Confirmed

claim_text: 1984 says it is an operator of essential services under Iceland's NIS law and is working with CERT-IS and outside specialists
summary: 1984 says it is "a designated operator of essential services under Icelandic NIS legislation" and is working with external specialists and CERT-IS while it restores services.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The status page says so in these words.

claim_text: Reykjavík City and the Blue Lagoon were also attacked on Nov 25; no source we read links either attack to 1984
summary: Vísir reports Reykjavík City's systems were attacked on Nov 25 and the Blue Lagoon reported an attack the same day. A CERT-IS official said he could not be sure those two were related. RÚV says the Reykjavík attackers used Microsoft Azure.
detail: Vísir quotes the CERT-IS official saying the Blue Lagoon and Reykjavík attacks share some similarities that need closer study. Vísir mentions the attack on 1984 only as having happened the week before; neither outlet says Reykjavík City or the Blue Lagoon used 1984 or were reached through it, and 1984 has named no customers.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Vísir quotes CERT-IS comparing only the Reykjavík and Blue Lagoon attacks, and RÚV says the Reykjavík attackers used Microsoft Azure; neither links them to 1984.
notes: Whether the attacks are connected is not known.

claim_text: An Icelandic pro-Palestine association says it believes Israel was behind the attack; it gives no evidence
summary: RÚV reports a statement from the Iceland-Palestine Association (Félagið Ísland-Palestína) saying it believes Israel is behind the attack, which it calls an attack on Iceland's sovereignty. It offers no evidence of its own.
detail: The association is an advocacy group, not an investigator. 1984 has named no country, and no official body has said who did it.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: RÚV reports the association's statement, quoting it: the association 'telur Ísraelsríki standa að árásinni' (believes the state of Israel is behind the attack).

claim_text: RÚV reports that at least three Icelandic websites supporting the Palestinian cause were destroyed in the attack
summary: RÚV reports that at least three Icelandic websites declaring support for the Palestinian cause were destroyed in the attack on 1984. The Iceland-Palestine Association says the attack was aimed at seven websites supporting Palestine.
detail: RÚV does not name the sites. It links a separate report that the association's own website may be ruined after a cyberattack.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: RÚV says 'Minnst þrjár íslenskar vefsíður þar sem lýst er yfir stuðningi við málstað Palestínumanna voru eyðilagðar' (at least three Icelandic websites supporting the Palestinians' cause were destroyed).

claim_text: The founder of the cryptocurrency service Wagyu blames the 1984 attack for a $13.5 million sell-off of its XMR1 token; 1984 said it did not know whether data had leaked
summary: Vísir reports that Wagyu's founder wrote that the key that issues XMR1 was on an old 1984 server he had deleted, but its files were still there. 1984's managing director said on Nov 20 it did not know whether data had leaked.
detail: Vísir, citing the crypto outlet Decrypt, says XMR1 fell more than 99% in about half an hour on Nov 20 after 5.2 million tokens were sent to a new account, which sold about 364,000 of them to 388 buyers for $13.5 million. This is the founder's claim; no investigator has said the key was taken from 1984. 1984 later said customer-hosted data was not accessed except on the seven targeted sites (c003). The Hacker News discussion (s010) is where readers raise this question; it is not evidence of anything.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Vísir reports the founder's post that the key was on an old server he had deleted while 1984 kept its files, and quotes 1984's director: 'Við vitum ekki raunverulega hvort að þarna varð gagnaleki' (we don't know if data leaked).
